title: Greed as idolatry; empty words; fellow-partakers; darkness to light (Eph 5:5–8)
english: to have in the kingdom of Christ and God, he names on their own, and says, "Let it not even be named among you." Then, in a place of its own, set apart from the earlier ones, he adds shamefulness, foolish talk and coarse joking.

Earlier we supposed that "greed" was put for adultery. So let us ask, from the words "or a greedy person, who is an idolater," whether that reading is overturned or can still stand. Now we have found that in many places the prophets call idolatry fornication, as in "they went whoring after their idols." And one could also take fornication to stand for idolatry, from the saying, "By a spirit of fornication they went astray" (Hosea 4:12). But if the greedy person is the one who gets money for himself from where he ought not, greed is called idolatry because those who love money are, as it were, worshipping the images engraved on the coins; for along with the coins these people love, as it were, the images stamped on them too. And I think the apostle somewhere also calls the love of money idolatry.

"Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of this the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience" (Ephesians 5:6). Origen says: He seems to call "empty words" the words that try, by some show of persuasion, to overturn the teaching about the punishments brought on those who have lived wickedly. At any rate he says that such words belong to deceit and are empty, because the wrath of God spoken of here will certainly come upon the sons of disobedience. He calls the disobedient "sons of disobedience," as though the vice of disobedience became a mother and bore them, so that they carry, as it were, their mother's likeness. In the same way one can find in many places of the Scriptures "sons" and "children of fornication," "sons of death," "sons of Gehenna" and other phrases like these.

"Do not, then, become fellow partakers with them" (Ephesians 5:7). Note the words "partaker" and "fellow partaker." Perhaps "partaker" is said of the better and "fellow partaker" of the worse. So, for example: "Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your partakers" (Psalm 45:7), and, "For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence firm to the end" (Hebrews 3:14). I do not remember "fellow partaker" being used anywhere except in the present passage; but here it is clear that the fellow partaker belongs to the worse.

"For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord" (Ephesians 5:8). If what was once darkness can change and become light, there are no natures doomed to perish. Just as the righteous are the light of the world, so the ungodly might be called darkness. The righteous, being light, will see light in light; but the unjust, being darkness, are a people sitting in darkness, seeing nothing. By their fruits we shall recognize who is light and who is darkness. For everyone who does evil hates the light, and, not coming to the light, he is darkness, a son of darkness and of night; but whoever does the truth comes to the light, and he is light, a son of light and of day (John 3:20-21). Besides this, consider whether "but now you are light in the Lord" is said of the righteous because there are some lights that are not in the Lord. It was especially fitting that the Ephesians, enlightened in the light of knowledge, should be told, "but now you are light in the Lord."
"Walk as children of light" (Ephesians 5:8). If God is light and there is no darkness in him at all, then the children of God are children of light.

"For the fruit of the light is in all goodness and justice and truth" (Ephesians 5:9). These words are useful against those who separate the just from the good, and who think that the Creator is just, but that the one they imagine above him is the good God. For the fruit of the light is in goodness and in justice and in truth. Where there is goodness, then, there is justice; and where there is truth, there is justice. But goodness and truth are with the good Father; so justice too is with him and not with another.
